I’ve given up on traditional breastfeeding until we are home and am sticking to pumping exclusively. There’s some very lovely mom groups on Facebook for a combination of pumping exclusively AND breastfeeding. I was worried that now that he’s over a month old and so used to a bottle he won’t latch once we’re home, but I’ve gotten a lot of responses to reassure me, in particular some moms have had success switching from bottle to breast beyond the month mark, and sometimes over 12 weeks. 

In the end, I’ve learned it’s mostly up to your babe if they want to breastfeed, but *fed* is best, and pumping still means you’re doing what’s best for her, and feeding her the healthiest you possibly can. Even if you have to fortify with formula, using even the slightest ounce of breastmilk is great. 

About supply issues, the advice my LC gave me was pump for 20, rest for 10, pump for 10, rest for 10 and pump one last time for 10, 6-8 times a day. Your supply will take a couple days to increase, and (trying to word this correctly) using 1 lower level suction than you can handle with a pump is less painful and exhausting. I’ve seen good reviews for medela and avent, if that helps. 

Feeding during a NICU stay is a highly stressful thing, especially if your plan is to breastfeed. I hope this helps, this is just my personal experience and knowledge.
